subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 27-year-old woman presents with a malar rash, symmetric arthritis of the hands, and pleuritic chest pain. Antinuclear antibodies are positive at 1:640, anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies are negative, and anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein antibodies are detected. The rheumatologist explains that these antibodies recognize small nuclear ribonucleoproteins.
question: These autoantibodies most directly impair which of the following processes?

options.text: Capping of the 5-prime end of pre-mRNA
Polyadenylation of the 3-prime end of mRNA
Splicing of pre-mRNA by the spliceosome

explanation_correct: Small nuclear ribonucleoproteins are small nuclear RNAs bound to proteins such as the Smith antigen; they assemble into the spliceosome, which cleaves pre-mRNA at the 5-prime and 3-prime splice sites and removes introns. Anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein antibodies are associated with systemic lupus erythematosus and mixed connective tissue disease.

explanation_incorrect.A: 5-prime capping adds 7-methylguanosine cotranscriptionally and does not require the spliceosome.
explanation_incorrect.B: Polyadenylation at the AAUAAA signal is performed by poly-A polymerase, not by small nuclear ribonucleoproteins.
explanation_incorrect.D: Aminoacylation is catalyzed by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, each specific for one amino acid and its tRNA.
explanation_incorrect.E: Assembly of the 40S initiation complex is mediated by eukaryotic initiation factors (eIFs), not by small nuclear ribonucleoproteins.

educationalObjective: snRNPs assemble into the spliceosome that removes introns from pre-mRNA, and anti-U1 snRNP autoantibodies are associated with SLE and mixed connective tissue disease.
